newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Ringgit recovers but sentiment remains weak.
newsitem.headline: Ringgit recovers but sentiment remains weak.

text.p: * Ringgit recovers from lows on profit-taking of dollar positions
* Sentiment remains weak after sell-down by speculators
* Bank Negara heard checking rates through agent banks
The ringgit recovered from its lows in early Asian trading on profit-taking of dollar positions, dealers said.
But ringgit sentiment remained weak after recent sell-down by speculators, dealers said.
At 0200 GMT, the ringgit was at 2.5880/5930 to a dollar after earlier hitting 2.5930, its weakest level since August 1994.
"Ringgit remains weak and only profit-taking is limiting its fall," said a dealer with a large Malaysian bank. "But trading is thin due to large spread of 30 to 50 points."
He said the large spread was also exaggerating rate movements.
Dealers said dollar/ringgit might test the 2.6000 level later on Friday or early next week.
"With Bank Negara not providing much resistance, I think funds will try to push dollar/ringgit toward 2.60," said a European bank dealer in Kuala Lumpur.
Malaysia's central bank was heard checking rates through agent banks this morning, dealers said.
The ringgit's undertone remains bearish due to a perceived change in stance by Malaysian authorities.
Acting Prime Minister and Finance Minister Anwar Ibrahim said on Tuesday that Malaysia would allow the exchange rate to be determined by market forces.
The statement was interpreted that the authorities were willing to tolerate further ringgit weakness.
